elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY” for matters arising under or related to the Agreement.

elements.element: The fee limb consists of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly uses “fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap equals the greater of the 12-month fee limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause caps liability at “THE GREATER OF (A)” the specified fee limb “AND (B) USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: “NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT ... DAMAGES.”

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: “NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY ... CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES.”

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to “EITHER PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY” obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to either party's breach of its “DATA PROTECTION” obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to either party's breach of its “SECURITY OBLIGATIONS.”

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to either party's “INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.”

elements.element: Either party's liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out excludes either party's “GROSS NEGLIGENCE” from the cap. The earlier TrueLink-specific parenthetical is redundant but does not negate the later mutual carve-out.

elements.element: Either party's liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out excludes either party's “WILLFUL MISCONDUCT” from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out excludes either party's “FRAUD” from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out excludes “ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS” from the cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Customer's payment obligations, being Client's obligations to pay all amounts due under this Agreement, are not damages.” The Customer/Client terminology is awkward, but the appositive expressly identifies the relevant Client payment obligations.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The cap equals 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is not simply 12 months' fees; it is the greater of 12 months' paid-or-payable fees and USD 1,000,000. There is no evidence that the 12-month fees will always equal or exceed USD 1,000,000, so the additional floor may change the cap.

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to either party's indemnification obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: The foregoing cap does not apply to either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Either party's liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The mutual carve-out expressly includes either party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Either party's liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The mutual carve-out expressly includes either party's willful misconduct.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred mutual cap, greater-of quantum, mutual damages exclusion, all specified uncapped carve-outs, and payment-obligation treatment. It does not independently satisfy the fallback's exact 12-month-fees quantum because of the USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing Client indemnity remains effective. Drafting is substantively clear but retains a redundant, TrueLink-specific gross-negligence parenthetical and inconsistently uses “Customer” and “Client.”
